newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sunken Panamanian ship spews oil off SAfrica coast.
newsitem.headline: Sunken Panamanian ship spews oil off SAfrica coast.

text.p: About 200 penguins were rescued along South Africa's Indian Ocean coast after a sunken Panamanian freighter spilled its oil fuel, officials said on Wednesday.

"There are 200 penguins that have been brought ashore covered in oil. We are expecting more to come through as the rescue operation continues," said Claire Ward, from a Cape Town-based marine life group attending to the birds.
Police spokesman John Fobian, also involved in the clean-up operation, said a dead seal had beached near Port Alfred.

"The sea around here is full of oil patches which are now being deposited on the sand. We have handled a couple of seals and penguins that swam in the oil," he said. "There is one seal that has died."
Marine biologist Victor Cockroft said the spillage was serious for the coastline's penguins.
"This looks like the worst spill (yet) for the penguins because the ones I have seen are very, very oiled. It is possible that a number are going to die," he said.
Ninety percent of the ship's 800-tonne oil fuel has spilled out to sea from the wreck of the 12,000 tonne Cordigliera.

The freighter sank in rough seas off Port St Johns on South Africa's Wild Coast on November 14 with its crew of 29 and its cargo of steel, granite and paper. An operation to remove the oil is continuing.
